• Scientific name: Noturus gladiator Thomas & Burr, 2004
  • Common name: Piebald Madtom
  • Size: 107 mm (4.2") SL
  • IUCN Red List: Near Threatened (last assessed 2012)

North America: coastal plain streams of Tennessee and Mississippi, USA. Gulf Coast drainages, Mississippi. Type locality: just upstream of Potters Creek, about 2.5 km west of Bolivar, Pleasant Run, Hatchie River at Summerville-Bolivar Road, Mississippi River basin, Hardeman County, Tennessee, U.S.A.
Breeding: unreported. There is no breeding report.

Etymology: from the Greek notos, meaning back, and oura, meaning tail, in reference to the confluent adipose and caudal fins. The specific epithet refers to the large, serrated pectoral spines (gladiator = swordsman).
Ichthyological Exploration of Freshwaters v. 15 (no. 4), pp 353, Figs. 2-3, 8c.
